verdict.rationale: PostHog's own docs say it is open-source and offers a free Docker Compose self-host deployment under an MIT license, so the product does provide self-hosting. The evidence is a single short doc statement, and an early hands-on report found the production Dockerfile broken, so how complete and production-ready the self-hosted core is remains unproven. missing for 10: documentation of which core features are available when self-hosted, production-scale self-host guidance (scaling, upgrades, support), current independent or hands-on confirmation that the Docker Compose deployment works.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: PostHog is open-source and freely available for anyone to host themselves. We offer a free Docker Compose deployment under an MIT license.
We offer a free Docker Compose deployment under an MIT license.
